en: Homage to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas! Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling among the Śākyas, in Kapilavastu, in the Nyagrodha Grove.
Now at that time, Prince Rāhula had gone to his bed, and a certain rākṣasī [approached him].

Prince Rāhula was terrified. Then, at the end of that night, surrounded and escorted by many young princes, he departed from Kapilavastu and approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and stood before him weeping.
Thereupon the Blessed One addressed the venerable Ānanda:

"Take up, Ānanda, the protective spell of the youth Rāhula called Mekhalā; we shall explain it. Listen to me, O hosts of gods, hosts of nāgas, hosts of rākṣasas, hosts of asuras, hosts of garuḍas, hosts of gandharvas, hosts of kinnaras, hosts of piśācas, hosts of kumbhāṇḍas, hosts of pūtanas, hosts of grahas, hosts of nakṣatras, and the twenty-eight great yakṣa generals!"
The four great kings, the worms free from passion, those dwelling in the Himavat mountains, the beings who reside in the ten directions, and the hosts of rākṣasīs: Pākiḍi, Laṃbodarī, and Kīṭakarṇī.
And Sumanā, Mahārati, and the hosts of Mothers who are the protectors of the one who is like the ocean; in the eastern quarter is the rākṣasī named Hari;
in the southern quarter is the rākṣasī named Goṇāsī; in the western quarter is the rākṣasī named Kesari.

In the northern direction there is a rākṣasī named Mahācūḍā; these are the terrible rākṣasīs, each surrounded by sixty koṭis [of followers]. May they constantly provide protection for Prince Rāhula and for the Mekhalā-vidyā; may they protect, protect me, Gornikṣiṇa, and provide protection for Niveditā. It is as follows: ghane ghane ghane ghane.
Ghaphu Ghanapati! Ghume ghume!
Ghume!
Wandering, wandering, wandering, O Lord of Wanderers!
In every house, in every house, in every house!
O Master of the House, O Destroyer of the House!
Lord of arrows, lord of wealth,
lord of gods,
non-harming, lord of non-harming.
Mamati, Amati, Sumati.
O Lord of the Multitude, *hala hala hala*!
*Hala hala*!
*Hala halam halapa*!
hili hili hili hili hili hili / hili / hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu hulu /
tili tili tili tili tili tili tili //
Ṣiṭi ṭape ṭaṭṛpe / olaṃbe mavisāre / haha hihi huhu /
Samatasare / Asamaṃtacare Palikhasare / Acarte /
O Ānanda, this girdle, the *Samantapratisarā* known by the name *Ānandamekhalā*, is a powerful spell that shall never be obstructed by Vidyādharas,

Bhūtas, or Vetālas, even those of great strength, supernatural power, and great heroism. O Ānanda, this girdle-spell was spoken by the Blessed Buddhas for the benefit and happiness of sentient beings.
...up to [its use] for protection, praise, and concealment;
and other great ones have spoken of this girdle, O Mekhalānanda, which brings benefit to all sentient beings:
whoever there may be who are evildoers, who feed on vital energy (*ojas*), [they shall be overcome].
They dwell upon the earth.

Having heard this Mekhalā-vidyā, they flee in every direction, terrified. Ānanda, having well-mastered this Mekhalā-vidyā, protect, protect Prince Rāhula! I shall provide protection for my cowherd son on all sides for an area of twelve yojanas.

I provide protection, support, and guardianship; I perform rites for peace and well-being; I effect the avoidance of punishment; I effect the avoidance of weapons; I neutralize poison; and I repel enemies.
I perform the binding of the boundary; I perform the binding with thread.
I ward off all malevolent beings. Whether humans or non-humans, let no evil ones cause harm; svāhā!
Having performed the ritual service by bowing to the Tathāgata and offering flowers and incense, one should perform the binding with a thread,
as well as the massaging, the sprinkling, and the wiping, [with the thought]: "May there be the warding off of all planetary influences and the pacification of all diseases."
Namely: nile nile / vimale tamale / hiri bhiri siri masara svāhā //

Upon hearing this spell, the entire earth trembled; the hosts of spirits shook, and the hosts of gods assembled. The Naga kings assembled, the Bhūta kings assembled, and the Brahma-indras and Maheśvaras also assembled. Both Kumāras likewise assembled, and whatever beings have been mentioned, they all assembled at Mekhalā.

Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya said this to the Blessed One: “Blessed One, I shall provide protection for the young prince Rāhula; I shall grant him refuge, acceptance, and guardianship, as well as peace, auspiciousness, immunity from punishment, immunity from weapons, the neutralization of poisons, the warding off of enemies, the binding of boundaries, and the binding with cords—all these being the attendants of the Mekhalā-vidyā.”
Namely: acaṭanī caṭanī ... culu culu / ūrdhvadaṇḍe adhardaṇḍe samantadaṇḍe /
Nimi-mune / Śānti / (MDh_GBM 3253.1) ... it is impossible that they should find an opportunity [to harm];
setting aside their ancient karmic obstructions, may there be well-being.
...from human fears, from all human fears,
svāhā!
There, indeed, the Blessed One—

...the spell named [so-and-so], together with its retinue. This, Ānanda, is the Mekhalā spell; it binds the clouds, the winds, and the storms. It is not to be transgressed by a god, a nāga, a yakṣa, or a rākṣasa.
by a śramaṇa or a brāhmaṇa,
or by a caraka or a parivrājaka;
Or by a Kāpālika:
the knowledge of the *mekhalā* destroys for everyone [the effects of] *kṛtya*,
*khākhorda*, and *vetāḍa*.
The knowledge composed by Śramaṇas cuts [the bonds];
the knowledge composed by Brāhmaṇas cuts;
the knowledge composed by Carakas cuts.
It cuts through the spell performed by the Aṅgas;
it cuts through the spell performed by Maheśvara;
[it cuts through] the great [spell] performed by Śakra.
...the Lord; the knowledge produced by the moon, the sun, the planets, and the constellations; [and that produced by] the gods, nāgas, and yakṣas...
The spell performed by those possessing supernatural powers (*ṛddhimant*) cuts [the spell].
The spell performed by Śā... cuts the spell.
... cuts [the spell].

This knowledge of the girdle (*mekhalā-vidyā*) severs what is made by mountain peaks, what is made by the earth, and what is made by the sky; it is the supreme severance of all [obstacles]. This is the knowledge of the girdle.
I do not, Ānanda,
permit [this]; I perform a boundary-binding for the sake of peace and well-being.
He bestows a retinue, namely:
Kele, Makela, and Kāmakela.
Ḍare / ḍamare / At that time, the four great rākṣasīs provide a retinue for the Meḳhalā-vidyā.
... *hiri*, *śānti*, I perform the rite of auspiciousness (*svastyayana*) until I perform the binding of the boundary (*sīmābandha*); *svāhā*. [He] offers the *arivāra* [oblation], namely: *dadare*.
Daddare / haha hihi huhu / ... vaṭṛ /
Ṭara ṭara / rakra makṛ kaju / dṛ dṛ dṛ /
dū dū dū / himi limi / tṛpetṛti / drahiti /
He bestows,
he gains;
he grants protection, defense, and guardianship.
I perform the neutralization of poison and the warding off of enemies until I establish the boundary;
whoever [attacks], I establish that boundary for him.
May no one cause me harm, svāhā! Whoever...
Whether it be a *pūtana*, or a *kaṭapūtana*, or a *garuḍa*, or a *kinnara*, or a *mahoraga*;
whether it be a *skanda*, or a *dvaitīyaka*, or a *traitīyaka*, or a *cāturthika*; whether it be a human or a non-human—[none of these can harm one who has mastered this].
